newsitem.title: USA: ING buys Equitable of Iowa for $2.2 billion.
newsitem.headline: ING buys Equitable of Iowa for $2.2 billion.

text.p: Equitable of Iowa Cos., which specialises in annuities and life insurance, said Tuesday it agreed to be acquired by Dutch financial services company ING Groep NV in a deal worth a total $2.2 billion.
ING will acquire 130-year-old Equitable of Iowa for $68 a share, offering its stockholders cash or ING American Depositary Shares. It also will assume $400 million in Equitable debt.
The deal reflects the ongoing consolidation in the U.S. insurance industry as companies seek to expand their product offerings, distribution channels and regional markets.
"It's not a surprise," Douglas Meyer, fixed income analyst for Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co., said of the deal. "The broader financial services industry is consolidating."
Fred Hubbell, chairman of Des Moines-based Equitable of Iowa, said the deal was aimed at enhancing revenue growth and not cutting costs to boosts profits.
"We believe this transaction is designed to create top-line sales opportunity," Hubbell said in a telephone interview. "The transaction is not based on cutting expenses to improve profits."
After the merger, Equitable will expand distribution of ING's life insurance products, particularly through a network of banks and brokerages, Hubbell said.
In addition, Equitable's portfolio of fixed and variable annuities will bolster ING's life insurance product offerings.
"There are significant cross-selling synergies between the two businesses just to begin with," Hubbell said.

Equitable markets fixed and variable annuities and fixed and variable life insurance products through independent insurance agents, banks and broker-dealers. ING is involved in banking, insurance and asset management on a global basis.
The Equitable deal is ING's largest takeover to date, but the Dutch banking and insurance company still plans to expand further in the United States and Europe.

ING Executive Chairman Aad Jacobs said the Amsterdam-based company's ambition to be one of the top 10 life insurance companies in the United States had not been satisfied by the acquisition, which put it only into the top 20.
Jacobs also said ING was working hard to expand in corporate banking in Europe, particularly in Germany and France, and it still intended to buy a U.S. investment bank.

Equitable's stock jumped $8.375, or 15 percent, to $65.75 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the biggest percentage gainers. ING's U.S. shares rose $2.94 to $51.19, also on the NYSE. Hubbell declined to
comment on a possible competing bid for Equitable, but said he believed the ING offer was a "very attractive package of values" for shareholders, employees and customers.

However, from the time ING first approached Equitable in late 1996 or early 1997 until the present other companies had also expressed an interest in possibly acquiring Equitable, Hubbell acknowledged. He declined to give details.
"I really can't comment on that," Hubbell said. "Certainly, there have been other companies that have expressed an interest during that same period of time."
Hubbell reiterated that prior to agreeing to be acquired by ING Equitable was not for sale.
Beyond financial terms, ING's offer was attractive based on the Dutch company's commitment to growth and a similar corporate culture, he said.
"If we were going to find a partner, we wanted to align ourselves" with a strong company, Hubbell said.
The merger is expected to close by the end of 1997, subject to customary conditions, inculding regulatory and Equitable shareholder approval.
There is no connection between Equitable of Iowa, founded in 1867, and The Equitable Cos. Inc., a New York-based financial services and insurance company.

Equitable of Iowa will retain its name and corporate autonomy, although it will be part of ING Financial Services International North America. The unit also includes Life of Georgia, Security Life of Denver, The Southland Group and The Netherlands Insurance Co.
As part of the deal, Hubbell will join the ING FSI North American general management team as president and chief executive of the expanded retail life and annuity businesses.
In addition, Equitable of Iowa board members will be invited to join the ING North America Insurance board.
